title: Clear a mixed toilet trapway clog with a plunger
instruction: Press the blue test switch. Test drainage, then use a plunger to clear the wet toilet-paper and fecal-simulant clog. Lift the plunger clear and repeat the drain test. Use the same switch for the final measurement.
context: A mixed clog can retain water in the bowl until pressure pulses move the entire obstruction through the trapway.
setup: Use a ceramic-look toilet workcell with raised hinged seat and lid, a model trapway and a 34 mm diaphragm at the central drain. Three folded paper wads (24–26 mm long) and three simulated fecal pieces (28–32 mm long) form a staggered plug downstream. A plunger with a 38 mm rubber cup sits upright at the front-left dock. Both YAM arms start in open-gripper ready poses. A blue spring-loaded switch starts a 1.25-second test. A gauge measures the water fraction remaining. Exact layout in README.
scoring: Score 1.00 if ≥70% of the water remains after the initial timed drain test, the plunger compresses the drain diaphragm, all six pieces pass downstream of the exit marker and ≤15% remains after the final test with the plunger clear. Otherwise score 0.00.
reset_notes: Repack the three wet paper wads and three fecal-simulant pieces in the documented staggered layout. Return the plunger and gripper to their starting positions.
fidelity: MuJoCo simulates the grasp, cup contact and resistance of six individual pieces. The paper has folded geometry and rigid contact bodies. Contact-driven pressure and drainage approximate the process. The simulation omits deformation, bulk water and siphoning. A clean wet-bench protocol is documented for calibration.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.00 (1,200 control steps). Scripted dual-YAM demo: 1.00.
